title: ME LD517: An Act Regarding Synthetic Media in Campaign Advertising

obligations: A person operating a broadcast, cable or satellite system within this State must include an oral or written visual announcement of each disclosure required by this section when broadcasting a public communication described in subsections 1 to 2-A, except as provided in subsection 5-C, paragraph C (Sec. 1, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3)

A newspaper must include each disclosure required by this section when publishing a public communication described in subsections 1 to 2-A, except as provided in subsection 5-C, paragraph C (Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B)

Whenever a public communication that requires a disclosure under subsections 1, 2, 2-A or 2-B contains synthetic media, the public communication must include the words "THIS COMMUNICATION CONTAINS AUDIO, VIDEO AND/OR IMAGES THAT HAVE BEEN MANIPULATED OR ALTERED." in addition to any other required disclosure (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)

The commission shall adopt rules regarding the manner, size and placement of the disclosure required under subsection 5-C; these rules are routine technical rules as defined in Title 5, chapter 375, subchapter 2-A (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
prohibitions: A person operating a broadcast, cable or satellite system within this State may not broadcast any public communication described in subsections 1 to 2-A without an oral or written visual announcement of each disclosure required by this section, except as provided in subsection 5-C, paragraph C (Sec. 1, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3)

A newspaper may not publish a public communication described in subsections 1 to 2-A without including each disclosure required by this section, except as provided in subsection 5-C, paragraph C (Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B)

A public communication that requires a disclosure and contains synthetic media must include the required synthetic media disclosure; failure to do so is a violation subject to penalty (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C; Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4)
reading.what_it_does: This law requires public communications in Maine campaign advertising that already require a disclosure and contain synthetic media to include a specific warning that the audio, video and/or images have been manipulated or altered. It defines synthetic media, exempts satire, parody and certain clarity modifications, and limits broadcaster and newspaper liability to cases of actual knowledge. Violations can lead to civil penalties up to 500% of the expenditure and injunctive relief by the Attorney General.
key_definitions: synthetic media: an image, an audio recording or a video recording depicting a candidate's appearance, speech or conduct that (1) in a manner that is likely to deceive a reasonable person, depicts the candidate saying or doing something that the candidate did not say or do, or (2) has been manipulated or altered in a manner that is likely to provide a reasonable person with a materially different understanding or impression of the candidate's appearance, action or speech than a reasonable person would have from an unaltered, original version of the image, audio recording or video recording; synthetic media does not include modifications to improve clarity, add captions or highlight a specific section as long as the modification does not create a materially different understanding or impression, and does not include satire or parody (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶A and ¶B)

newspaper: any printed material intended for general circulation or to be read by the general public, including a version of the newspaper displayed on a website owned or operated by the newspaper (Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B)

Determine whether the communication contains synthetic media as defined, including whether it depicts a candidate saying or doing something not actually said or done, or is manipulated to give a materially different understanding, and whether any exclusion for clarity modifications, captions, highlighting, satire or parody applies (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶A and ¶B)

If synthetic media is present, include the exact disclosure words "THIS COMMUNICATION CONTAINS AUDIO, VIDEO AND/OR IMAGES THAT HAVE BEEN MANIPULATED OR ALTERED." in addition to any other required disclosure (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
Follow the commission's rules on manner, size and placement of the disclosure once adopted (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)

If using a broadcaster or newspaper, ensure the required disclosure is included in the communication because the broadcaster or newspaper must include each disclosure required by this section, and they are only exempt from synthetic media liability if they lack actual knowledge (Sec. 1, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3; Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B; Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶C)

Persons operating broadcast, cable or satellite systems within Maine (Sec. 1, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3)
Newspapers, including printed material intended for general circulation and website versions (Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B)
The Commission on Governmental Ethics and Election Practices (Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4; Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)

Synthetic media does not include satire or parody (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶B(2))

A broadcaster or newspaper does not violate subsection 5-C unless it broadcasts or publishes a paid public communication with actual knowledge that it contains synthetic media; a third party allegation alone does not constitute actual knowledge (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶C)

In assessing a civil penalty, the commission shall consider how widely the public communication was disseminated, whether the violation was intentional, whether the violation occurred as the result of an error by a printer or other paid vendor, and whether the public communication conceals or misrepresents the identity of the person who financed it. If the person who financed the public communication or who committed the violation corrects the violation within 10 days after receiving notification from the commission by adding the missing information, the commission may, except for a violation of subsection 5-C, decide to assess no civil penalty. The commission shall notify the Office of the Attorney General if a person in violation of subsection 5-C does not cease violating after being notified by the commission or if the commission is unable to notify the person. The Attorney General may bring a civil action in the Superior Court of Kennebec County for injunctive or other appropriate equitable relief requiring compliance with subsection 5-C, and may combine that action with an action under section 1004-B for enforcement of penalties assessed by the commission. If the Attorney General prevails, the court may award costs and reasonable attorney's fees. Subsection 5-C may not be construed to prohibit or limit any other cause of action that a person may have against a person who violates subsection 5-C. The statute does not create a new private right of action, but preserves other causes of action. (Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4; Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶D and ¶E)

Passed 2026-03-19. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This law requires public communications in Maine campaign advertising that already require a disclosure and contain synthetic media to include a specific warning that the audio, video and/or images have been manipulated or altered. It defines synthetic media, exempts satire, parody and certain clarity modifications, and limits broadcaster and newspaper liability to cases of actual knowledge. Violations can lead to civil penalties up to 500% of the expenditure and injunctive relief by the Attorney General.

Who it applies to

  • Any person who finances or disseminates a public communication that requires a disclosure under subsections 1, 2, 2-A or 2-B and contains synthetic media (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
  • Persons operating broadcast, cable or satellite systems within Maine (Sec. 1, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3)
  • Newspapers, including printed material intended for general circulation and website versions (Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B)
  • The Commission on Governmental Ethics and Election Practices (Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4; Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
  • The Office of the Attorney General (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶D)

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • synthetic media: an image, an audio recording or a video recording depicting a candidate's appearance, speech or conduct that (1) in a manner that is likely to deceive a reasonable person, depicts the candidate saying or doing something that the candidate did not say or do, or (2) has been manipulated or altered in a manner that is likely to provide a reasonable person with a materially different understanding or impression of the candidate's appearance, action or speech than a reasonable person would have from an unaltered, original version of the image, audio recording or video recording; synthetic media does not include modifications to improve clarity, add captions or highlight a specific section as long as the modification does not create a materially different understanding or impression, and does not include satire or parody (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶A and ¶B)
  • newspaper: any printed material intended for general circulation or to be read by the general public, including a version of the newspaper displayed on a website owned or operated by the newspaper (Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B)

Obligations

  • A person operating a broadcast, cable or satellite system within this State must include an oral or written visual announcement of each disclosure required by this section when broadcasting a public communication described in subsections 1 to 2-A, except as provided in subsection 5-C, paragraph C (Sec. 1, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3)
  • A newspaper must include each disclosure required by this section when publishing a public communication described in subsections 1 to 2-A, except as provided in subsection 5-C, paragraph C (Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B)
  • Whenever a public communication that requires a disclosure under subsections 1, 2, 2-A or 2-B contains synthetic media, the public communication must include the words "THIS COMMUNICATION CONTAINS AUDIO, VIDEO AND/OR IMAGES THAT HAVE BEEN MANIPULATED OR ALTERED." in addition to any other required disclosure (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
  • The commission shall adopt rules regarding the manner, size and placement of the disclosure required under subsection 5-C; these rules are routine technical rules as defined in Title 5, chapter 375, subchapter 2-A (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)

Prohibitions

  • A person operating a broadcast, cable or satellite system within this State may not broadcast any public communication described in subsections 1 to 2-A without an oral or written visual announcement of each disclosure required by this section, except as provided in subsection 5-C, paragraph C (Sec. 1, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3)
  • A newspaper may not publish a public communication described in subsections 1 to 2-A without including each disclosure required by this section, except as provided in subsection 5-C, paragraph C (Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B)
  • A public communication that requires a disclosure and contains synthetic media must include the required synthetic media disclosure; failure to do so is a violation subject to penalty (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C; Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4)

Penalties and enforcement

Enforcement is by the Commission on Governmental Ethics and Election Practices and the Attorney General. A violation of this section may result in a civil penalty of no more than 100% of the amount of the expenditure in violation, except that a violation of subsection 5-C may result in a civil penalty of no more than 500% of the amount of the expenditure in violation, and an expenditure for yard signs lacking required information may result in a maximum civil penalty of $200. In assessing a civil penalty, the commission shall consider how widely the public communication was disseminated, whether the violation was intentional, whether the violation occurred as the result of an error by a printer or other paid vendor, and whether the public communication conceals or misrepresents the identity of the person who financed it. If the person who financed the public communication or who committed the violation corrects the violation within 10 days after receiving notification from the commission by adding the missing information, the commission may, except for a violation of subsection 5-C, decide to assess no civil penalty. The commission shall notify the Office of the Attorney General if a person in violation of subsection 5-C does not cease violating after being notified by the commission or if the commission is unable to notify the person. The Attorney General may bring a civil action in the Superior Court of Kennebec County for injunctive or other appropriate equitable relief requiring compliance with subsection 5-C, and may combine that action with an action under section 1004-B for enforcement of penalties assessed by the commission. If the Attorney General prevails, the court may award costs and reasonable attorney's fees. Subsection 5-C may not be construed to prohibit or limit any other cause of action that a person may have against a person who violates subsection 5-C. The statute does not create a new private right of action, but preserves other causes of action. (Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4; Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶D and ¶E)

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying AI generated or manipulated media in a Maine campaign public communication that requires disclosure under subsections 1, 2, 2-A or 2-B must include the exact disclosure "THIS COMMUNICATION CONTAINS AUDIO, VIDEO AND/OR IMAGES THAT HAVE BEEN MANIPULATED OR ALTERED." in addition to other disclosures (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
  • The definition of synthetic media covers images, audio or video depicting a candidate saying or doing something not actually said or done, or manipulated to give a materially different understanding or impression, if likely to deceive a reasonable person (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶A)
  • Violations of the synthetic media disclosure requirement can result in civil penalties up to 500% of the amount of the expenditure in violation, and the 10 day correction safe harbor does not apply to subsection 5-C violations (Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4)
  • The Attorney General may seek injunctive or equitable relief to compel compliance, and a court may award costs and attorney's fees to the Attorney General (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶D)
  • Broadcasters and newspapers are not liable for a synthetic media violation unless they have actual knowledge that the public communication contains synthetic media; a third party allegation alone does not constitute actual knowledge (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶C)
  • Satire or parody and modifications that only improve clarity, add captions or highlight sections without creating a materially different understanding are excluded from synthetic media (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶B)

Notable exemptions

  • Synthetic media does not include an image, audio recording or video recording modified to improve clarity, add captions or highlight a specific section, as long as the modification does not create a materially different understanding or impression (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶B(1))
  • Synthetic media does not include satire or parody (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶B(2))
  • A broadcaster or newspaper does not violate subsection 5-C unless it broadcasts or publishes a paid public communication with actual knowledge that it contains synthetic media; a third party allegation alone does not constitute actual knowledge (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶C)
  • For violations other than subsection 5-C, if the person corrects within 10 days after notification by adding missing information, the commission may decide to assess no civil penalty (Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4)
  • Yard signs lacking required information are subject to a maximum civil penalty of $200 (Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4)

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the public communication requires a disclosure under subsections 1, 2, 2-A or 2-B of 21-A MRSA §1014 (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
  • Determine whether the communication contains synthetic media as defined, including whether it depicts a candidate saying or doing something not actually said or done, or is manipulated to give a materially different understanding, and whether any exclusion for clarity modifications, captions, highlighting, satire or parody applies (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶A and ¶B)
  • If synthetic media is present, include the exact disclosure words "THIS COMMUNICATION CONTAINS AUDIO, VIDEO AND/OR IMAGES THAT HAVE BEEN MANIPULATED OR ALTERED." in addition to any other required disclosure (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
  • Follow the commission's rules on manner, size and placement of the disclosure once adopted (Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C)
  • If using a broadcaster or newspaper, ensure the required disclosure is included in the communication because the broadcaster or newspaper must include each disclosure required by this section, and they are only exempt from synthetic media liability if they lack actual knowledge (Sec. 1, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3; Sec. 2, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§3-B; Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶C)
  • If notified by the commission of a violation, cease the violation immediately; note that the 10 day correction safe harbor does not apply to subsection 5-C violations (Sec. 3, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§4; Sec. 4, 21-A MRSA §1014 sub-§5-C, ¶D)

 reasonable person with a materially different understanding or impression of the
 candidate's appearance, action or speech than a reasonable person would have from

 B. For purposes of this subsection, "synthetic media" does not include:
